title: The territory
summary: What is known of the world's places, on one grid of hexagons and on the ground: its people, lights, built-up land, settlements and urbanisation, from the whole Earth to a metropolis, each with the scale it means something at, each drawn in place.

layers.title: where people live
layers.about: The world's people in 2025 on hexagons of the H3 grid: each column as tall as the square root of its density. GHS-POP R2023A, binned here. Hexagons of resolution 2 from orbit, finer as one comes near.

layers.title: poverty at $3 a day
layers.about: The share of each economy's people below the international poverty line, in its latest survey (World Bank PIP). A mosaic of the hexagons the economy's people live in; where no survey stands, nothing.

layers.title: inequality (Gini)
layers.about: The Gini index of each economy's income or consumption, in its latest survey (World Bank PIP).

layers.title: people, 2015–2030
layers.about: People on the cells of H3 resolution 6 (about 36 km²), for any part of the world, through Space2Stats: WorldPop's estimates and projections, year by year. Drawn wherever one looks, up to a country at a time.

layers.title: urban centres and suburbs
layers.about: The share of each cell's people in urban centres, dense clusters and suburbs: the Degree of Urbanisation (GHS-SMOD R2023A) through Space2Stats.

layers.title: degree of urbanisation, 1 km
layers.about: GHS-SMOD R2023A for 2025 on the ground about the city: urban centre, dense and semi-dense clusters, suburbs, rural clusters and low-density land.

layers.title: settlement spreading, 1985–2015
layers.about: The World Settlement Footprint Evolution: the year each 30 m cell first stood built, seen from Landsat. With the scale of years above the clock, the city grows on the ground.

layers.title: night lights, 2012–2024
layers.about: The sum of VIIRS night-time lights on each cell, year by year, through Space2Stats: where activity has grown or dimmed.

layers.title: built-up land, 1975–2030
layers.about: The built-up surface on each cell every five years (GHS-BUILT-S R2023A), through Space2Stats; 2025 and 2030 are projections.

layers.title: river floods, by return period
layers.about: How deep a river flood of a chosen return period reaches, anywhere on Earth, on a grid of about 90 m (GloFAS, CEMS). The sea and small streams are not in it.

layers.title: people in flood zones
layers.about: People on each cell living where a 1-in-100-year flood reaches over 15 cm (Fathom with WorldPop, through Space2Stats).

layers.title: tropical cyclones
layers.about: How often tropical cyclones pass, averaged over each cell (through Space2Stats).

layers.title: landslide susceptibility
layers.about: Each cell's mean susceptibility to landslides (through Space2Stats).

layers.title: drought
layers.about: The depth of a 100-year drought at 1.5 °C of warming, on each cell (SPEI, through Space2Stats).

layers.title: wildfires
layers.about: Each cell's mean density of fires (through Space2Stats).

layers.title: the Earth by night
layers.about: NASA's Black Marble over the whole Earth, whatever the hour. Without the night layer the same lights show only on the night side, as the clock's Sun leaves them.

layers.title: built volume by hexagon
layers.about: The city's buildings binned on H3 cells of a resolution one chooses, each column the volume they enclose. The same grid as the world's, down to the blocks.

tools.title: Any indicator on the globe
tools.about: Search the World Bank's Data360 by what an indicator means, and raise it over the economies on the globe.

tools.title: A composite of place
tools.about: Your own index of a region, cell by cell: the factors Space2Stats holds, each scaled to 0–5, by weights you set; the columns follow as you move them.

tools.title: Sources and what stands behind them
tools.about: Each tool and dataset this workbench draws on, what was taken from it, and what could not be taken and why.

source: GHSL (European Commission JRC), Space2Stats (World Bank), the World Settlement Footprint (DLR), NASA's Black Marble (via GIBS), the Poverty and Inequality Platform and Data360 (World Bank); the grid is physis's H3, the composite nomos's.
